_date: DERIVED — see game/calendar.ts. Level 2 is Wednesday 3 March 2027, which is collection day.
_teaching: Bins arrive on the one day they are legal. Every bin on this level is compliant — the player learns the object before they learn to cite it, and Level 3 (Friday) is where the same object becomes a finding. Also the first bounty: a missing-cat notice, with the cat somewhere on the round.
briefing: Collection day. Containers at the curb are within the window today. Weeds and fence condition remain live.
_cameos: Jake and Sam walk Gus past 4400; Casey and Jess walk Pellet past 4412. Second shift, second pair of couples — the street fills up with people the player has seen before rather than with more strangers.
story: Wednesday. Collection day on Bonerville, so half the street has bins at the curb.
That is permitted today. Article IX allows Tuesday and Wednesday. It does not allow Thursday, and residents are aware of this.
A notice has been posted on the route. The Association has authorised a finder's fee. This is not a compliance matter.

bounty.name: Chaz
bounty._sprite: The PHOTO on the notice, not how he is drawn in the yard — that comes off the packed animal sheet via `animal`. A still frame is right for a photograph and wrong for a cat you are meant to spot moving.
bounty.headline: Missing
bounty.label: Cat, gray — answers to Chaz
bounty._placement: Seeded per level across the lots listed below. Never the first lot of the round: the player needs to have read the notice before they can be expected to have found him.
bounty._flyer: Tacked to the top-left of the stage rather than stood in a yard. A notice is something you read once and carry with you for the round; a prop in one lot is something you walk away from.
bounty._roams: He WANDERS the lot rather than sitting in a yard slot. A still cat is a spot-the-difference; one that moves has to be found — and the lot he is on may also have its own animal out, which is the whole point.

lots._teaching: Bins introduced on a lot with nothing else wrong. They are at the curb, it is Wednesday, and that is allowed. First lot of the round, so Chaz is never here.

decoys.why: R-104 permits containers at the curb on Tuesday and Wednesday. Today is Wednesday.
Same window. The bins are the point of the lot and they are compliant.

lots._teaching: Compliant bins next to a real weed finding, so the new object sits beside a known one without becoming it.

violations.why: Unbordered weed growth in the front turf.

lots._teaching: The screening decoy, and the sting in it: the bins are stored behind the fence, which makes them compliant on ANY day — and the fence they are hidden behind is itself a finding. Two objects, opposite answers, and the broken one does not contaminate the other.

violations.why: Members missing and displaced — gaps and uneven heights along the panel.

decoys.why: Screened from the right-of-way, which R-104 treats as compliant on any day — and the state of the screening is not part of that test.

lots._teaching: A clean lot with no bins at all. Absence is also information: not putting them out on collection day is not a violation of anything.
Close on a straightforward weed finding with compliant bins, so the round ends on the discrimination rather than on a new idea.
